body:
How projection works today

I read materialize_to (solace-cli/src/main.rs:1097). The modules aren't written to a separate generated directory. They go in place into the project's own src/ and test/, next to files people own, such as api.mjs, main.mjs and the FFI. For every module in the index, it:
writes src/<module>.gleam (or test/…), but only when the content on disk differs;
skips a file that was changed outside Solace (D-58). That file gets read back in on the next command instead;
records every file it wrote in a Written ledger (outside::Written).
It never deletes anything. A file with no module behind it stays where it is. The other half of the problem is delete (line 2321): it retires one symbol, and nothing ever retires a module.
Why "wipe and regenerate" doesn't fit

There's no directory Solace fully owns. Clearing src/ before writing would delete the FFI .mjs files and anything edited outside Solace that hasn't been read in yet. That second case is exactly what D-58 protects.
What I'd build: prune what Solace owns

The ledger already lists every file Solace wrote, so Solace can clean up its own files without touching anyone else's.
Retire empty modules. When delete removes a module's last symbol, it also retires the module, as long as no other module imports it. Also allow delete <module>, refused (like E5001) while something still imports the module. That covers the case where the module has an import or a module comment but nothing else.
Prune during materialize. For each file in the ledger with no module behind it:
if the file is unchanged since Solace wrote it, delete it and drop it from the ledger;
if someone edited it, leave it and report it, so a person's work is never deleted.
Rollback. transaction already writes everything back from the store after a rollback. With step 2 it would also remove files belonging to modules the rolled-back change had created.
Stale build output. build/dev/javascript/solace_board/solace_view.mjs can stay after its source is gone. I haven't checked whether gleam build removes it, so either check that or have prune drop the matching compiled .mjs too.
Tests. Add a Rust unit test in the style of delete_refuses_a_used_symbol_…: delete the last symbol, check that the module and the file are gone, and check that a file edited by hand survives the prune and gets reported.
title: Prune during materialize
